---
title: "Interpreter Startup"
description: "Control how Python and R interpreters start in Positron. Learn about automatic detection and workspace-based interpreter selection."
---

## First run

When Positron starts for the first time in a new workspace, it will start a Python and/or R interpreter session based on your workspace characteristics and whether there is evidence of RStudio being used recently.

Python starts right away in a folder that has Python files or a project environment.
For which Python starts, see [Which Python starts](python-installations.qmd#which-python-starts).

R starts right away in a folder that has R files, such as `.R`, `.Rmd`, `.Rproj`, or `renv.lock`.
Positron starts your system's current R version.
If you have no current R, or Positron cannot use it, Positron starts the highest R version that it can use.
If you set [`positron.r.interpreters.override`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.override), Positron starts the highest R version in that list.

See the [Python discovery](python-installations.qmd) and [R discovery](r-installations.qmd) guides for more information on language-specific installations.

### RStudio detection

Positron tries to start R for R users and Python for Python users by checking to see if RStudio is installed and has been recently used. The latter check is done by looking in `~/.local/share/rstudio` for files written less than a month ago. If you do not want Positron to consider you an RStudio user, remove this folder or rename it.

## Subsequent runs

When Positron starts in a workspace that has been used before, it will start the same language interpreter that was running the last time you used the workspace.

In the case of R, there is some additional subtlety.
When Positron records which R version was most recently used in a workspace, it also notes whether that R version is the system's current R version.
In subsequent runs, Positron launches the system's current R version, even if that is a different version number from the last-used R version.
We believe this behaviour is the least surprising for most users.
If you want to use a different R version in a workspace, select it once, and Positron starts it in future runs.

To choose which interpreter Positron starts in a folder, in place of the one you used last, set [`python.defaultInterpreterPath`](positron://settings/python.defaultInterpreterPath) or [`positron.r.interpreters.default`](positron://settings/positron.r.interpreters.default).

If Positron starts an interpreter you don't need, just delete the session, and that interpreter will no longer start automatically in that workspace.

To make Positron forget the interpreter it remembers for a folder, run _Interpreter: Clear Saved Interpreter_ from the Command Palette, then choose the language.
This command does not stop a running console.
If you keep using that console, Positron remembers its interpreter again, so shut the console down first.

## Implicit startup

In addition to starting up an interpreter session when the workspace is first opened, Positron will also automatically start an interpreter session when it looks like one is needed. For example, a Python session will start:

- When you open a `.py` file
- When you execute Python code

## Configuring interpreter startup

The [`interpreters.startupBehavior`](positron://settings/interpreters.startupBehavior) setting controls when Positron starts an interpreter on its own.
It does not change which interpreter starts.
To choose which interpreter starts, see [Which Python starts](python-installations.qmd#which-python-starts) and [R installations](r-installations.qmd).

### Choose a value

| If you want Positron to | Use |
|---|---|
| Start the interpreter you used last in a folder, or start one when you open a file or run code | `auto` (the default) |
| Start an interpreter every time you open a window, even in a new folder | `always` |
| Start the interpreter that the language suggests for the folder, not the one you used last | `recommended` |
| Start an interpreter only when you choose one or run code | `manual` |
| Never start the language, and hide its interpreters | `disabled` |

### What each value does

The interpreter that the language suggests is the one that [First run](#first-run) describes.

| Value | Folder you used before | New folder | Open a file | Run code | Choose from the **Interpreter picker** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `always` | Starts the interpreter you used last | Starts the suggested interpreter, if there is one | Starts the interpreter you used last, or the suggested one | Starts the interpreter you used last, or the suggested one | Starts the interpreter you choose |
| `auto` | Starts the interpreter you used last | Starts the suggested interpreter if the folder has files for that language | Starts the interpreter you used last, or the suggested one | Starts the interpreter you used last, or the suggested one | Starts the interpreter you choose |
| `recommended` | Starts the suggested interpreter if the folder has files for that language | Starts the suggested interpreter if the folder has files for that language | Starts the suggested interpreter | Starts the suggested interpreter | Starts the interpreter you choose |
| `manual` | Does not start | Does not start | Does not start | Starts the interpreter you used last, or the suggested one | Starts the interpreter you choose |
| `disabled` | Does not start | Does not start | Does not start | Does not start | Not listed |

Opening a file or running code starts an interpreter only when no session of that language is running.

### Set a value for one language

In the Settings UI, search for `@lang:r interpreters.startupBehavior` or `@lang:python interpreters.startupBehavior`, and choose a value.
A value for one language takes precedence over the value for all languages.

For example, if you only ever use Python and never want R to start, set `@lang:r interpreters.startupBehavior` to `"disabled"` to hide R interpreters from the Positron UI altogether. You can specify this at either the user or workspace level, and your configuration will appear in your `settings.json` as:

```json
{
    "[r]": {
        "interpreters.startupBehavior": "disabled"
    }
}
```
Alternatively, if you are mainly an R user, but occasionally use Python, you can set `@lang:python interpreters.startupBehavior` to `"manual"` to prevent Python interpreter sessions from starting automatically. This still allows you to start a Python interpreter session manually:

```json
{
    "[python]": {
        "interpreters.startupBehavior": "manual"
    }
}
```

To set one value for all languages, find the [`interpreters.startupBehavior`](positron://settings/interpreters.startupBehavior) setting in the Settings UI without a language key, and choose a value.
